subject: ISV runtime gateway compatibility: adapter checklist & pilot milestones
messages:
From: Aaron Liu <aaron@prompttools.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Gomez <elena@bridgecons.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runtime gateway compatibility — initial matrix attached

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As discussed, we pulled together an initial compatibility matrix that maps PromptTools' runtime gateway hooks to Redwood's serving runtime extension points. The goal is to confirm whether we can avoid a deep runtime fork and instead ship an "adapter shim" that sits between the customer's runtime and Redwood's batching/cache layers.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Redwood exposes the KV cache invalidation hook (we see an HTTP endpoint in the docs but want to be sure of semantics).
- Clarify tracing header passthrough (we currently rely on X-Trace-ID and need guarantees on propagation across model fallbacks).
- Performance constraint: adapter adds <10ms median overhead at 8k token sequences; we can tune after initial pilot.

I've attached: compat_matrix_v1.xlsx (mapping), and a tiny patch that shows the adapter's expected handshake (redwood-adapter-reference.patch).

Proposed pilot: 2-week sandbox integration -> 2-week joint perf run (small traffic) -> production enable by end of Q3. Are you able to confirm lanes and next-step contacts?

Thanks,
Aaron
Partner Engineering
PromptTools

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Runtime gateway compatibility — initial matrix attached

Aaron — appreciate the comprehensive pack. I skimmed the matrix and patch; good work. A few quick clarifications from our side to make the pilot lower friction: 

1) KV cache invalidation: Redwood exposes a transactional cache invalidation API (POST /v1/cache/invalidate) that supports prefix and key-level ops. Semantics: invalidation is asynchronous but provides a 200 + event id; then the runtime guarantees eventual consistency across the serving pool. For your adapter we recommend emitting invalidation requests with the event id tracked in the adapter for 60s; that should avoid stale-prefix races.

2) Tracing: we forward X-Trace-ID and set X-Redwood-Span for each model call. If you need full OpenTelemetry context propagation, we can enable OTLP over HTTPS inside the sandbox (requires a brief config flag).

3) Performance: the <10ms target is reasonable. We suggest starting with the shim in front of the batching layer (adapter -> redwood-runtime) rather than deep instrumentation inside the runtime; that reduces risk for the pilot.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: own the implementation checklist and runbook with PromptTools.
- Jonas: own perf instrumentation and verify tracing semantics during the perf run.
- Aaron/Elena: provide a minimal sample (Docker image or repo) that reproduces request/response handshake + tracing headers.

Can Marissa and Jonas confirm availability this week for a 45-min tech kickoff (we'll invite our infra SRE too)? Aaron/Elena, if you can drop the sample repo link into the thread that will speed us up.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Partnerships & Integrations
Redwood Inference
